notes:
1. BI → Chart: a new "AI Chart" button sits above "Add to dashboard". Describe the chart you want in the AI sidebar and it renders straight onto the BI chart builder — where it can be tweaked and added to the dashboard like any other visual. Charts generated from the Analyze tab keep landing there as before.
2. Colour Explorer template (analyze-color-data): both ΔE reference dropdowns now show the LD sample NAME instead of the item code, so picking a reference no longer requires knowing the LD_item.

1. Settings → AI: a new "Saved settings" dropdown sits right under the Enable AI switch and lists every configuration you have saved. Picking one refills the whole form — provider, endpoint, API key, model and temperature — so switching between providers is one click instead of retyping. Each Save refreshes its entry in the list, and up to 20 are kept.

1. AI assistant: a new Chat tab answers general questions — explanations, calculations, "what does this app do" — with no database or editor context attached. The sparkle button in the top-right corner opens it directly.
2. Results grid: right-click a cell or a column header for a new menu — copy a cell / row / selected rows, filter by or filter out a value, open or clear a filter, sort or clear the sort, pin a column left or right, autosize one column or all of them, reset columns, and hide or show columns. The grid had no right-click menu before.
3. Results grid — Copy fixed: it used to copy every row even when you had selected a few, and in some cases only the first row landed in Excel. It now copies exactly the rows you selected, or the whole result when nothing is selected, and Excel pastes it into real rows and columns. The button is also just "Copy" now.
4. Results grid — small numbers: values below 1 (for example 0.05) are no longer rewritten as a percentage ("5%"). Numbers are shown as they come back from the database, with thousands separators and up to 4 decimals.
5. Results grid — a "?" icon next to the AI edit button opens a short guide to everything the table can do: built-in features (double-click a header to rename it, Shift+click headers to sort by several columns at once) and the ones added on top (data types, add column, AI edit, revert).
6. Settings → AI: saving says the assistant picks the new settings up on your next message, and choosing a provider/model that already has a key on file restores that key straight away.

1. Settings → AI: AI now starts enabled by default, so "Ask AI" and the AI summaries work as soon as you add a provider and a key. Turn the master switch off if you do not want it.
2. Settings → About: the "Server / Shut down server" card has been removed. Closing the last tab already stops the app, and clicking your odbcapp:// bookmark starts it again.
3. "How to use this app": the first step now spells out the first-time setup — double-click ODBCQueryApp.exe once to register the odbcapp:// link, then save that link as a bookmark and use it from then on.

1. The version number is now shown in small print under the app name in the top-left corner, so you can tell which build you are running without opening Settings.
2. Feedback badge: a post you have read stays read. Read state is remembered per machine by post id, so it also survives updates and restarts instead of re-flagging old posts as unread.
3. Settings → AI: "Use saved API key" now fills in the brand and model that the saved key actually belongs to, rather than only the key itself.
4. AI chat (SQL, script and chart assist): added Volcengine and MiMo as providers, each with its latest flash model.
5. Script page → templates: expanding a template row now shows the columns it requires, the columns it can use optionally, and a list of what the script outputs.
6. Script page → templates: a new Example output column links to a sample dashboard for the template, which opens in a new window so you can see the result before running anything.
7. Script page → templates: the last column is now just the icon — the "Use template" wording has been dropped.
8. New script template "Machine uptime" for the FAB_MESA10 connection, built from the mesa_rsc_downtime / v_fab_mesa_dt_codes / mesa_resource_master query. Plant defaults to B180 and it comes with plant, mes_resource and event_start_date as default criteria; mes_resource shows 180L26C as an example. It produces an uptime dashboard with planned and unplanned downtime percentages, a status timeline, duration histograms and a gravure-change analysis.
9. Test Components: the analysis picker in the left panel is now single-select, so you choose one analysis instead of ticking several.
